transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-11-02
- Time: 09:30 PT
- Duration: ~60 minutes
- Attendees: Lina (AE), Marcus (SE), Diego, Renee, Joey (Enablement), Priya (PMM), Asha (Growth), Ben (Sales)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough): Rapid role-play of messaging plus short demo run. Lots of micro-edits; aim to produce short public demo clip.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Lina): Alright uh let's kick off, thanks everyone for joining. Quick agenda, three 90-second messaging rounds, then a 7-minute demo kitchen run where Marcus will show the KV cache + fallback routing example.
00:18 Speaker 2 (Marcus): Yep, I'll start with a short run of the hosted pitch, then flip to dedicated and private. Expect to see the throughput numbers and an on-call fallback example.
00:30 Speaker 3 (Joey): One ask - can we emphasize the 'developer-first' angle and how it maps to ramp time. Customers always ask 'how long till we ship' and they want simple answers.
00:45 Speaker 1 (Lina): Good call. Ok 90-second round one, you two, Marcus you go with hosted.
01:05 Marcus (SE): Sure. Hosted API: Redwood offers simple REST/SDK, streaming, function calling, and pre-curated models. We position this for quick time-to-value, low ops—so say, teams that want to ship chat or retrieval augmentation in days not months. Latency is typically X-100ms to X-200ms depending on size, and we show token-level cost breakdowns in the console.
01:32 Priya (interrupting): Can you call out the free credits / quickstart templates? That's an important close.
01:37 Marcus (SE): Right, free credits, SDKs, and templates for node/python. Also integration examples with vector DBs.
01:46 Lina: Nice. 90-second feedback: shorter lead-in, start with value — "ship in days, lower ops" then stats.
02:05 Marcus: Got it. Round two, Dedicated capacity - I'll try the cost/throughput angle.
02:18 Marcus: Dedicated: reserved GPUs, predictable throughput, autoscaling policies, SLA-backed latency targets. Ideal for high-throughput inference where you need isolation. Talk about burst capacity and commit pricing. Key objection we see: "isn't dedicated expensive?" Answer: show unit economics and how batching and KV cache reduce per-token cost. Also mention rollouts/canaries.
02:55 Renee (field engineer): Quick note: when they ask about private deployments, call out KMS and on-prem option early.
03:05 Marcus: Yep, will do.
03:20 Lina: Round three: Private / VPC pitch.
03:25 Marcus: Private deployments: private control plane, customer-managed networking, HSM/KMS integrations, audit logs. For regulated industries we recommend private with optional on-prem package. Talk about data residency.
03:42 Asha (Growth): We need a one-liner for regulated buyers: something like "deploy behind your VPC with optional on-prem package and KMS for keys".
03:50 Diego: Also say 'same API, same ops' — that's a big differentiation.
03:55 Marcus: Good.
04:10 Speaker 1 (Lina): Now let's do the 7-minute demo kitchen. Marcus, pretend the customer is a fraud detection team with bursty inference. Start with the hosted route and then show fallback to a smaller quantized model when capacity spikes.
04:30 Marcus: Starting demo - loading the sample app. Uh the demo script is in the deck not the live site, but I'll run the pre-recorded steps. (faint keyboard sounds)
04:50 Marcus: Step one: send a request to the hosted endpoint - response streams back incremental tokens. Note we show token-level trace in the console, you can see the latency breakdown per model.
05:10 Ben (Sales): Quick Q: how do you show cost during the demo without leaking internal numbers?
05:15 Marcus: Use the demo mode console which shows normalized cost per token; we can also switch to an anonymized benchmark sheet.
05:28 Marcus: Now emulate a capacity spike. Our smart routing policy routes requests to a compatible model variant — for example a 7B quantized variant with slightly lower quality but much lower latency/cost.
05:50 Priya: Do we have a good line for "quality vs cost tradeoff"?
05:55 Marcus: Yes, "We provide model variants tuned for cost and latency with measurable quality deltas; we help you pick the right tradeoff through tooling and evals."
06:08 Marcus: Showing KV cache: when the same prefix is used, token generation hits the cache and latency drops from ~150ms to ~20ms for repeated queries.
06:30 Asha: That cache stat is gold, we should put it on the one-pager.
06:40 Marcus: Noted. Now the canary/rollback demo: we push a new model variant to 10% traffic; the console shows error and quality monitors, and we automatically fallback if regression detected.
06:58 Marcus: End of demo run - any live questions?
07:05 Joey: Audience question we often get: "what audit logs exist at token level?" How do we answer?
07:12 Marcus: Answer: We capture request/response metadata, have per-request tracing hooks and long-term retention available as an add-on. For regulated customers we offer SOC 2-level logs and integration with SIEMs.
07:28 Priya: Another common: SSO and RBAC?
07:32 Marcus: Support for SAML/SSO, SCIM, RBAC in console — and customer-managed encryption keys via KMS/HSM.
07:40 Renee: There's sometimes confusion between "private control plane" and "on-prem package". Suggest we preface with a sentence: "Private = control plane in your network; on-prem = full runtime in your datacenter."
07:58 Marcus: Good wording.
08:10 Interrupt (murmur):
08:12 Marcus: Ok, let's roleplay objections. Ben you'll play the procurement skeptic: "Your competitor does something similar for cheaper."
08:25 Ben (as prospect): "We can get a cheaper per-token rate elsewhere, why Redwood?"
08:30 Lina (AE role): Short close: "Cost matters, but predictability and integrated ops reduce your unplanned spend. With Dedicated you get commit pricing and predictable throughput, and Optimize gives batching and quantization recs to lower costs further while keeping quality."
08:46 Ben: Good, but a buyer will say 'show me numbers'.
08:50 Marcus: Offer to run a short benchmark on their workload; we can run an apples-to-apples cost/latency test and share a spreadsheet. That usually buys us time.
09:05 Priya: On competitor rebuttals: for Anthropic - push our developer workflows and model catalog strengths; for OpenAI - highlight deployment flexibility and private options; for Hugging Face - stress the unified runtime and SLA.
09:28 Diego: Add a line about 'we own the inference stack optimizations' — kernel selection, batching, and KV cache — that helps rebut the 'we're just a wrapper' critique.
09:40 Marcus: Let's do one lightning pitch cycle where each of us has 45 seconds to sell Redwood to an engineering leads. Ready?
09:48 Lina: I'll go first. (45s) "Redwood helps engineering teams ship LLM features with predictable latency and unit economics. You get a unified API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so you can start with hosted and later pin dedicated capacity without rewriting code. We provide observability and rollouts to reduce regressions and optimize model choices for cost and quality."
10:35 Marcus: (45s) "We focus on production inference: optimized runtime, KV cache, continuous batching and smart routing. That translates to lower per-token cost and better tail latency for production apps. Plus we provide canary rollouts and automatic fallback to keep availability high."
11:20 Diego: (45s) "From an SRE viewpoint: we integrate with KMS/HSM, support VPC peering, and offer audit logs for compliance. For on-prem regulated stuff, we can ship an air-gapped package."
12:05 Joey: Great. Let's capture the crisp lines and build a 1-pager.
12:12 Priya: Also record a short demo clip that highlights KV cache and fallback routing, that's our top marketing artifact for Q4.
12:20 Action item interjection: Lina to do messaging 1-pager, Marcus demo clip.
12:30 Speaker 4 (Renee): One demo troubleshooting note: when you demo fallback to quantized model, call out small expected quality diffs and show the eval numbers.
12:45 Marcus: We'll show evaluation scores from our eval harness - not raw prompts.
13:00 Asha: For the sales playbook, add a checklist: stakeholder map (eng, infra, security), timeline, success metrics (p95 latency, total cost of inference).
13:15 Lina: Yup. Ok last 8 minutes - rapid-fire objection handling. I'll throw quick objections, you answer.
13:25 Lina: "We need guaranteed latency of 50ms P95"
13:28 Marcus: "If you need 50ms P95 then we recommend a small Dedicated cluster pinned to that workload; we can also suggest quantized smaller models and aggressive batching settings."
13:45 Lina: "Can you deploy inside our VPC?"
13:48 Marcus: "Yes, private with customer control plane and network peering; for air-gapped we have an on-prem package."
14:02 Lina: "How do you rotate keys?"
14:04 Marcus: "KMS/HSM integrations with rotation policies, and we can document rotation process for compliance."
14:20 Priya: A quick note for messaging: avoid saying 'we're faster' — instead 'we provide predictable latency with tools to measure and tune' - that's more defensible.
14:35 Marcus: Good counsel.
14:40 Lina: Ok quick recap and next steps: 1) Lina will produce the messaging 1-pager, 2) Marcus will record the demo clip, 3) Priya will update competitor slides, 4) Joey will set up two demo kitchen sessions. We'll reconvene after artifacts are ready.
14:58 Ben: Any CRM tags for this?
15:02 Joey: Tag as 'enablement-demo-kitchen-Q4' in Confluence and attach to playbook.
15:10 End: thanks everyone.
